text:
sqlpipe is a three-stage pipeline that moves relational data from Postgres into S3 as Parquet, with each stage running as an independent process connected by bounded queues.

The reader process opens a server-side cursor against Postgres and streams rows in fixed-size batches, keeping memory flat regardless of table size and letting downstream stages apply backpressure.

The converter consumes these batches, maps Postgres types to a Parquet schema, and accumulates rows into columnar row groups, flushing each group once it reaches a target size to balance compression against memory.

The uploader takes completed row groups and writes them to S3 using multipart uploads. Each part is retried independently with exponential backoff, and a failed upload is aborted cleanly so no orphaned parts accumulate. Completed objects are committed atomically, so partial files never become visible to consumers.
